subject: Module signing & drift-detection playbook for private deployments

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia@datasecure.com>
Cc: DataSecure Procurement <procurement@datasecure.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Module signing & drift-detection playbook for private deployments

Hi all,

Following up from the security questionnaire, DataSecure asked for a clear playbook describing how we ensure Terraform/Helm/Ansible module integrity for private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. I put together a first draft that covers:
- artifact signing (cosign/in-toto for charts and OCI modules)
- git tag signing and provenance for terraform-module releases
- CI gating jobs for image/AMI/helm-chart signatures
- a lightweight drift-detection runbook that runs after deployment and on schedule

I've attached the draft playbook and a CI snippet with cosign examples. Please review technical gaps and also call out anything that would block DataSecure from an audit perspective.

Proposed quick agenda for a discovery call:
1) Verification primitives (cosign/in-toto vs. internal KMS signing)
2) CI changes required (build matrix and gating)
3) Drift detection signals and escalation path
4) Timeline for evidence deliverables they can consume (SLSA attestations, signed release artifacts)

Can we sync tomorrow for 30 min?

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Product Security (Private Deployments)
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 09:15 Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com> wrote:
> Following up from the security questionnaire...

Thanks Naomi — good init. A few practical notes from the infra side:

- Recommend we standardize on cosign for signing container/OCI chart artifacts and in-toto for provenance for multi-artifact releases. That keeps the tooling small and aligns with what our cloud partners accept.
- Terraform modules: publish versioned tarballs to our private registry with SHA256 + cosign signature; CI job terraform-module-release#prod should only promote when cosign sig present.
- Helm charts: push signed OCI chart blobs; Helm install pipeline must check signature with cosign before apply (helm plugin or OCI pull + cosign verify).
- Ansible roles/collections: publish to private ansible-galaxy index; record release SLSA attestation for the collection.
- Drift detection: propose a scheduled job (privinfra-drift-scan) that runs terraform plan (in read-only mode) + helm diff and produces a concise findings artifact. If any critical drift (security group, route, KMS policy) — auto-open INFRA-942 and notify owners.

I've crossed out anything that would require major platform work in the doc and added CI job names. See inline comments in the playbook. Happy to take the lead on CI snippets if we agree.

- Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer

Subject: Re: Module signing & drift-detection playbook for private deployments

Naomi — thanks for the fast turnaround and Aditya for the implementation notes. A couple of clarifying asks from our security/compliance team before we schedule the formal audit packet delivery:

1) Evidence format: can you produce SLSA 1/2 attestations for module releases and a machine-readable list of artifact signatures (artifact -> cosign sig)? We prefer both signed artifacts and an attestation bundle.
2) Drift detection frequency and retention: we need 90 days of runbook results and a mechanism to query findings by resource id.
3) Proof of verification in CI: we'll want to see pipeline logs (redacted) showing cosign verify steps and gate pass/fail for at least two releases.

If you can provide a short timeline and point to where we'll get these artifacts (Drive link or S3 signed URL), procurement will translate into contract language for the SOC/attestation clause.

Regards,
Alicia Gomez
Security Engineer, DataSecure
[No attachments]

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia@datasecure.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 18:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Module signing & drift-detection playbook for private deployments

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps below. Quoting Alicia's asks so we have a clear acceptance set for DataSecure.

Decisions/agreements:
- Tooling: cosign for artifact signing + in-toto for multi-artifact provenance.
- CI gating: terraform-module-release and helm-chart-release pipelines will require cosign signatures before promotion. Job names: terraform-module-release#prod, helm-chart-release#prod, ansible-collection-publish#prod.
- Drift detection: implement privinfra-drift-scan scheduled workflow (daily quick scan, weekly deep scan). Findings retained for 90 days in an internal bucket; CLI and API to query resource id -> scan results. Critical findings auto-open INFRA-942 and page oncall.
- Evidence delivery: we'll put attestation bundles and redacted pipeline logs in the shared Drive folder and provide signed URLs for DataSecure's auditors.

Action items (owners & ETA):
1) Aditya — implement cosign verify step in helm & terraform release jobs, provide example logs (ETA: 2026-02-24).
2) Jordan — wire up privinfra-drift-scan skeleton and create storage layout for 90d retention (ETA: 2026-03-05).
3) Naomi/Irene — prepare SLSA attestation template + mapping to our release flows and deliver initial bundle to Alicia (ETA: 2026-02-26).
4) Naomi — schedule 30-min sync with DataSecure for Feb 25; calendar invite to follow.

References: Drive folder with draft and CI snippets: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_privdeploy_playbooks
Jira for the automation work: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-942

Regards,
Irene Choi
